newsitem.title: UK: Italy local govt ratings may top sovereign - Moody's.
newsitem.headline: Italy local govt ratings may top sovereign - Moody's.

text.p: Italian local governments may attain domestic currency credit ratings which are higher than Italy's sovereign rating, Moody's Investors Service said in a report on Wednesday.
"Ratings of the Italian government's foreign-currency debt is constrained by Italy's sovereign ceiling, which is currently Aa3, because of currency transfer risks," Moody's said
"However, independence from central government transfers, political stability, and a city's ability to withstand economic shocks might allow lira-denominated debt to exceed that ceiling," it said.
Moody's cited Naples as an example.
The City of Naples holds a high investment grade rating from Moody's Investors Service (Aa3) despite being "in dissesto", which signifies financial distress, Moody's said.
"Under Italian law, debt service payments are senior to all other payments, including wages and salaries," a Moody's analyst said in the report.

This seniority is enforced by the requirement that an issuing municipality appoint a treasury bank to collect all revenues. The bank is given "irrevocable authority" to make interest and principal payments on all bonds and loans.
"The treasury bank is further required to allocate funds to ensure timely payments, and these funds are placed in trust accounts of the Bank of Italy," Moody's said.
"As a result, creditors do not incur credit or counterparty risk of the treasury bank, which is merely a paying agent for the city," the report said.

The Moody's analyst said these legal requirements are the real reason why not one of the roughly 400 Italian communities involved in dissesto proceedings has ever missed or delayed payment on verified financial obligations.

Naples' financial picture meanwhile has improved in the past two years because of the dissesto proceedings, the rigorous budget control process now mandated by law, and improved economic management, Moody's said.
